newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 26.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Agriculture Minister Josef Lux said it would be counterproductive for prices of agricultural products to be matched with those in western Europe. According to Lux such an increase would make Czech products less competitive.

- Premier Vaclav Klaus said it was a mistake to create joint stock companies where the state retained a stake. Klaus said that nations going through a similar economic transformation in the future should avoid the problem by transforming state-owned firms to private ownership as quickly as possible.

- Economists are skeptical on whether the government's decision to issue new bonds will encourage savings. Economist Jan Svejnar said that the rate of interest more than anything else will encourage people to buy the bonds.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Results from collective bargaining between key domestic industries and trade unions indicate that both sides have agreed that wages will grow at a much slower rate than last year. Firms such as CKD holding or Skoda Auto will increase wages from between two-four percent rather than seven percent as was the case last year.
- Large companies in the Czech Republic plan to continue downsizing. CKD plans to layoff 1,500 employees, while CEZ intends to downsize its staff by five percent of its 11,000-strong work force.

- Deputy Fincance Minister Vladimir Rudlovcak acknowledged yesterday that the finance ministry should share blame in the disappearance of 1.25 billion crowns worth of assets from CS Fond. Rudlovcak, however, would not admit whether his subordinates were negligent in allowing the incident to happen.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The Civic Democratic Party (ODS) welcomed member of parliament Tomas Teplik to its ranks. He was dismissed from the opposition Social Democratics last December. Teplik's crossing the floor now gives the ruling coalition 100 seats over the 98 seats controlled by the Social Democrats, Communists, and Republicans.

PRAVO - Premier Vaclav Klaus circumvented coalition partners yesterday when he struck an agreement with the leader of the official opposition, Milos Zeman to allow Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik to read before parliament a report on the status and execution of the nation's budget.
